summary: The stuck-run failure modes are now reproducible through the QA interface with zero prior knowledge: every new run's chat opens with a system message advertising the /qase-test command and its two subcommands. Sending them replays the unresponsive-runtime failure (run ends with the actionable shutdown error and status error) and the runtime-reuse block (any follow-up message on the quarantined runtime is rejected with the 'start a new run' guidance). No model call, no browser — deterministic every time.
what_was_done: Every new QA run now starts with a system message: 'Stuck-run repro available: send `/qase-test <unresponsive-runtime | runtime-reuse-block>` …' (commit 873f770)
The /qase-test command itself (previous round) applies the exact guarded faults through the same live-record path a real incident takes; it was previously only discoverable in source
what_was_tested: Created a fresh account, logged in through the real auth + CSRF flow, created a new run: the first chat message is the repro hint
Automated tests assert the hint appears on new runs and that both fault modes produce the expected surfaces
Full automated test suite: 505 tests, 0 failures

test_results.name: New run advertises /qase-test repro surface (live, real auth flow)

notes: Repro path: log in → create a new run → read the first system message → send /qase-test unresponsive-runtime → observe the actionable error and status error → send any follow-up message → observe the runtime-reuse rejection
